english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Keep an eye on bags in the 1866 Street market lanes and harborfront crowds in peak season, and expect rowdy nightlife around Korai Square late at night.

hood_desc: Old Town (Centro) is the historic heart around Lion Square and the Venetian harbor, packed with tavernas, museums, and nightlife, ideal for first-time visitors who want to walk everywhere and stay in the middle of the action.

Poros is a working-class seaside neighborhood just east of the center near the port, suited to budget-minded travelers who want quick ferry and airport access and a more local, everyday Cretan atmosphere.
Nea Alikarnassos is a practical residential suburb right by the airport with affordable hotels, good for one-night stopovers, early flights, or travelers prioritizing convenience over charm.
Mastampas is a quiet, largely residential district southwest of the center popular with locals, offering cheaper stays and an authentic neighborhood feel within a short bus ride or walk of downtown.
Ammoudara is a beach-resort strip just west of the city with a long sandy shoreline, hotels, and beach bars, best for families and sun-seekers who want the coast while staying close to Heraklion.

water.note: Safe in Heraklion and other major towns; bottled water recommended in smaller villages.

transit.pay: Buy paper tickets at kiosks/shops before boarding (cheaper) or from the driver onboard (pricier), or use the operator's app for e-tickets; KTEL intercity tickets (e.g. to Knossos) are bought separately at the bus station. A city ticket costs about €1.30 pre-purchased or €2.30 onboard (~$1.40-2.50).
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30am-10:30pm; there is no night service.
transit.note: Heraklion relies on KTEL intercity coaches plus a separate urban bus network - no metro or tram.

food.name: Dakos
food.desc: A hard barley rusk softened with olive oil, piled with grated tomato, crumbled mizithra cheese and oregano. Crete on a plate.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: Champions old Cretan recipes with its own farm produce; the city's standout restaurant.

places.name: Ippokampos
places.note: Long-running mezedopoleio by the water; locals queue for the meze and the prices.

food.name: Kalitsounia
food.desc: Little Cretan pastries filled with soft mizithra cheese or wild greens, baked or fried and finished with thyme honey.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: Makes both the sweet honey and the wild-greens versions from village recipes.

places.name: Fyllo...Sofon
places.note: Pastry specialists in the centre; good for kalitsounia and bougatsa to take away.

food.name: Gamopilafo
food.desc: Cretan wedding rice slow-cooked in goat and lamb broth then finished with staka butter. Rich, savoury and traditionally a feast dish.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: One of the few places in the city cooking it properly, with the meat served alongside.

places.name: Parasties
places.note: Creative Cretan cooking near the waterfront; ask what is on that day.

food.name: Bougatsa
food.desc: Flaky filo layered with sweet or sour mizithra cheese, cut with a knife, dusted with sugar and cinnamon and eaten for breakfast.

places.name: Kirkor
places.note: Heraklion's most famous bougatsa counter, on the central fountain square since the 1920s.

places.name: Fyllo...Sofon
places.note: The nearby rival, often with a shorter queue and equally good pastry.

food.name: Antikristo lamb
food.desc: Lamb splayed on stakes and cooked slowly facing an open fire, a shepherd's method that leaves the meat smoky and falling apart.

places.name: Ligo Krasi Ligo Thalassa
places.note: Cretan taverna cooking with grilled meats and raki, popular with locals in the evening.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: Cooks lamb and goat by traditional Cretan methods; book, especially in summer.

food.name: Apaki
food.desc: Pork marinated in vinegar then smoked over aromatic herbs and shrubs, sliced thin as a meze or folded into eggs and pies.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: Cures its own apaki; comes with rusks, cheese and a shot of raki.

places.name: Ippokampos
places.note: Classic meze plate of apaki and cheese to share over a carafe of wine.

food.name: Raki (tsikoudia)
food.desc: Clear Cretan pomace spirit poured at the end of every meal, usually free, usually with a plate of fruit or sweets.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: Serves village raki and rakomelo, the honey-warmed winter version.

places.name: Ligo Krasi Ligo Thalassa
places.note: Raki keeps coming with the meze; a proper Cretan evening rather than a tourist one.

food.name: Cretan wine
food.desc: Island grapes worth seeking out: crisp white Vidiano and Vilana, and the spicy red Liatiko and Kotsifali grown inland.

places.name: Ippokampos
places.note: House wine by the carafe plus bottles from small Heraklion-region estates.

places.name: Peskesi
places.note: All-Cretan wine list with staff who will match a grape to each meze.

landmarks: Palace of Knossos
Europe's oldest city and the labyrinthine heart of Minoan civilization, where 3,500-year-old frescoes, grand staircases and the Throne Room evoke the myth of the Minotaur.
Heraklion Archaeological Museum
The world's finest Minoan collection gathers the Phaistos Disc, bull-leaping frescoes and snake goddess figurines, essential context before or after visiting Knossos.
Koules Fortress (Rocca a Mare)
This stout 16th-century Venetian sea fortress guards Heraklion's old harbour, its ramparts carrying stone lions of St. Mark and sweeping Aegean views.
Venetian Walls and Tomb of Kazantzakis
Four kilometers of massive 16th-century ramparts encircle the old city, with writer Nikos Kazantzakis buried atop the Martinengo Bastion beneath his defiant epitaph.
Morosini Fountain (Lions Fountain)
Four marble lions have spouted water at the heart of Lions Square since 1628, the Venetian centerpiece of Heraklion's liveliest café crossroads.
Agios Titos Church
Dedicated to Crete's patron saint and rebuilt across Byzantine, Venetian and Ottoman eras, this elegant church houses the revered skull relic of St. Titus.
Venetian Loggia
Heraklion's most graceful Venetian building, a 17th-century Palladian arcade where nobles once gathered, now serves handsomely as the city hall.
Historical Museum of Crete
From El Greco paintings to the Battle of Crete, this superb museum spans seventeen centuries of Cretan history inside a neoclassical mansion near the seafront.
Agios Minas Cathedral
One of Greece's largest cathedrals, consecrated in 1895, lifts its grand dome over Heraklion in honor of the city's miracle-working patron saint.
Central Market on 1866 Street
This bustling market street brims with Cretan cheeses, mountain herbs, olive oil and raki, the tastiest introduction to the island's celebrated gastronomy.

train.note: The island of Crete has no railway of any kind, so there are no trains from Heraklion. Get around the island by KTEL intercity buses, and leave Crete by ferry or by flying from Heraklion airport (HER).

bus.note: As an island city, Heraklion has no international coaches. KTEL Heraklion–Lasithi runs domestic buses across Crete (Chania, Rethymno, Agios Nikolaos, the beaches). Official tickets: https://www.e-ktel.com/.

intl.to: Santorini, Mykonos, Paros & Naxos (Greece) - seasonal high-speed catamaran, Apr-Oct

ferry.note: Heraklion's ferries are all domestic but they are the main way off the island. Overnight ships sail year-round to Piraeus (Athens) with Minoan Lines and Blue Star Ferries; seasonal high-speed catamarans (SeaJets, Minoan, Blue Star) serve the Cyclades — Santorini, Mykonos, Paros, Naxos — roughly April–October. Book well ahead in summer. There are no direct international ferries from Crete.

half.name: Knossos Palace
half.blurb: The sprawling Minoan palace ruins are Crete's most celebrated archaeological site.

half.name: Spinalonga & Agios Nikolaos
half.blurb: A fortress islet and former leper colony reached from a pretty seaside town.

half.name: Rethymno
half.blurb: A Venetian old town of narrow lanes, a harbor lighthouse and a hilltop fortress.

half.name: Chania
half.blurb: Crete's most beautiful town wraps a Venetian harbor in atmospheric old streets.

half.name: Lasithi Plateau
half.blurb: A fertile mountain plateau dotted with windmills and the mythic Dictaean Cave.

half.name: Phaistos & Matala
half.blurb: Minoan palace ruins pair with a laid-back beach set beneath cave-pocked cliffs.
